method: The average split is the elapsed time multiplied by 500 and divided by the distance in metres, so 2,000 m in 7:00 is (420 x 500) / 2000 = 105 s, quoted as 1:45.0 per 500 m. The inverse multiplies the split by the distance and divides by 500, so a 2:00 split over 2,000 m is 8:00.0 and the same 1:45 pace over 5,000 m is 17:30.0. The per-1,000 m figure is twice the 500 m split. Average speed is the distance divided by the elapsed time in metres per second, shown also in km/h at 3.6 times that value. When a stroke rate is supplied, the stroke count is the rate in strokes per minute multiplied by the elapsed minutes and rounded to the nearest whole stroke, and metres per stroke divides the distance by that unrounded count. Times accept m:ss, h:mm:ss or plain seconds, with at most one decimal place; the time or split must fall between 10 s and 24 hours, the distance between 100 m and 100,000 m, and the stroke rate between 5 and 80 strokes per minute. A missing, malformed or out-of-range value is rejected with an actionable message rather than defaulted. Times are displayed rounded to the nearest tenth of a second, so a shown split can differ from the underlying average by up to 0.05 s. Every figure is an average for the whole piece: the standing start, sprint finish, current, wind, blade type and boat class are not modelled, and the stroke count assumes the entered rate held throughout. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Rowing pace convention: average time per 500 m, so a 2,000 m piece in 7:00 is 1:45.0 per 500 m.
Split and total time are proportional: split = time x 500 / distance, and time = split x distance / 500.
Distance per stroke is distance divided by stroke count, with strokes = stroke rate in strokes per minute x elapsed minutes.
